analyses.name: EOG Resources, Inc.
analyses.verdict: A fresh 52-week high reached with an RSI of only 53.5 - the rarest and most attractive combination on the entire 451-name scan, sitting on top of a balance sheet built to survive the cycle it is currently benefiting from.

financials.period: Last completed fiscal year (FY2025, ended December 2025)
financials.summary: EOG runs the most conservative financial model among the large US independents, and that model is what makes the current cycle profitable rather than merely busy. The company has spent years driving down per-well finding and development costs so the portfolio generates acceptable returns at crude prices well below where it currently trades, which means the geopolitical premium in oil flows to the bottom line rather than being consumed by cost inflation. Revenue growth of 58.7% against EPS growth of 109.4% shows the operating leverage in that structure: when the commodity moves, earnings move roughly twice as fast because the cost base is largely fixed. The balance sheet carries very low net debt relative to peers, which matters enormously in an industry where the last two downturns were survived or not survived on leverage alone. Free cash flow generation has been prioritised over production growth, funding a regular dividend, special distributions and buybacks rather than acreage expansion. The result is a company that does not need high oil prices to work but converts them very efficiently when they arrive.
highlights: Revenue +58.7% year over year
EPS +109.4% - roughly double the revenue growth rate, showing the fixed-cost operating leverage
Forward P/E of approximately 10.2x, among the lowest of any name scoring above 88 in the scan
Low net leverage relative to the US independent peer group - the defining structural advantage
Free cash flow prioritised for shareholder return over production growth

accomplishments: Reached a new 52-week high at 148.70 going into this session
Sustained a multi-year reduction in per-well development cost, lowering the corporate breakeven
Maintained a premium-drilling standard that screens out marginal locations rather than chasing volume growth
Continued returning capital through regular plus special dividends while peers levered up

The transformation came in the last several weeks as Middle East supply risk repriced the entire complex. What separates EOG's version of that move from the refiners' is its shape: TRGP, VLO and MPC went vertical with RSI readings of 71 to 79, while EOG walked to a new high with RSI at 53.5 - the market bid it without panic-buying it.

analyses.name: Occidental Petroleum Corporation
analyses.verdict: The only large energy name still 9.3% below its 52-week high while the sector prints new ones - the laggard with the most room, and a deleveraging story that finally has the cash flow to finish itself.

financials.period: Last completed fiscal year (FY2025, ended December 2025)
financials.summary: Occidental's financial story for several years has been the debt taken on to acquire Anadarko, and everything about the current setup is about that overhang clearing. EPS growth of 964.9% is arithmetically flattered by a depressed prior-year base, but the direction is the point: a highly levered producer in a strong crude tape converts revenue into equity value far faster than an unlevered one, because every incremental dollar of cash flow retires debt that sits ahead of shareholders. Revenue growth of 53.4% reflects both the commodity move and the scale of the combined Permian position. The company also carries a chemicals segment (OxyChem) that provides a genuinely counter-cyclical earnings stream, and a carbon capture business that is a long-dated option rather than a current contributor. A 15.1x forward multiple is a premium to EOG or FANG, and that premium is precisely the leverage - investors pay more per dollar of earnings because those earnings are geared.

Revenue +53.4%
Forward P/E of approximately 15.1x - a premium to unlevered peers, reflecting balance-sheet gearing
Debt reduction remains the primary use of free cash flow
OxyChem provides a chemicals earnings stream uncorrelated to upstream

accomplishments: Continued paydown of the Anadarko acquisition debt, materially reducing the leverage overhang

analyses.name: Eli Lilly and Company
analyses.verdict: A mega-cap growing revenue at 47.7% while sitting 0.7% from its 52-week high with an RSI of only 52.7 - growth at that scale without momentum extension does not normally exist.

financials.period: Last completed fiscal year (FY2025, ended December 2025)
financials.summary: Lilly's financial profile is the most unusual in mega-cap pharma: revenue growth of 47.7% at a company of this size is a rate normally seen only in early-stage businesses, and it is being driven by the incretin franchise - tirzepatide across diabetes and obesity indications - reaching genuine mass-market scale. EPS growth of 26.2% is lower than revenue growth, and that gap is deliberate: the company has been spending aggressively on manufacturing capacity because supply, not demand, has been the binding constraint. That capex is the right decision economically but it compresses near-term margin, which is why the earnings line lags the revenue line. The balance sheet supports the spending comfortably. The forward multiple of roughly 25.9x is the highest in large-cap pharma and is the market's assessment that this growth rate persists rather than reverting - the entire bull and bear argument sits in that one assumption.
highlights: Revenue +47.7% year over year at mega-cap scale - the standout growth rate in large-cap pharma
EPS +26.2%, deliberately trailing revenue as manufacturing capacity is built out
Forward P/E of approximately 25.9x - a premium the market assigns to franchise durability
Manufacturing capacity expansion is the primary capital allocation priority
Incretin franchise spans both diabetes and obesity indications

It has consolidated rather than corrected, and the rotation out of technology into healthcare has arrived just as that consolidation completed.

analyses.name: Johnson & Johnson
analyses.verdict: A 52-week high printed with an RSI of 57.4 on above-average volume - not a growth story, but the most orderly advance on the healthcare board and the natural destination for capital leaving long-duration technology.

financials.period: Last completed fiscal year (FY2025, ended December 2025)
financials.summary: J&J's numbers are deliberately unexciting and that is the entire investment argument. Revenue growth of 6.6% and EPS growth of -0.9% describe a business that is not accelerating - but they also describe one that is essentially immune to the two forces dominating this tape. Nothing about the pharmaceutical and medtech portfolio depends on AI capex, and its cash generation is real and near-term rather than discounted from distant years, which is exactly what protects it when Treasury yields rise and long-duration assets get repriced. The balance sheet is among the strongest in the entire equity market, with a AAA-adjacent credit profile that gives it acquisition capacity most peers lack. Following the consumer health separation, the remaining business is a cleaner pharmaceutical and medical device company with better growth characteristics than the headline rate suggests. At 22.0x forward earnings it is not cheap in absolute terms, but it is priced as an income-and-stability asset rather than a growth one.

analyses.name: Reinsurance Group of America, Incorporated
analyses.verdict: The best risk-adjusted name in the entire new leadership: 8.3x forward earnings with EPS up 159.6%, 2% from its high with RSI at 63.5, and a business model where the rising yields that are breaking technology are direct margin.

financials.period: Last completed fiscal year (FY2025, ended December 2025)
financials.summary: RGA's financial model is the cleanest expression of the rising-rate trade available in the equity market, and it is barely understood as such. A life reinsurer collects premiums today against claims that arrive over decades, and invests the difference. When Treasury yields rise, every dollar of that float reinvests at a higher rate, and because the liabilities were priced at lower assumed rates, the spread widens immediately and durably. That is why EPS grew 159.6% against revenue growth of 18.5% - the earnings expansion is not a volume story, it is an investment-yield story. The 8.3x forward multiple is the market applying an insurance-sector discount to what is, for the moment, a rate-leveraged earnings machine. The offsetting reality is that reinsurance books are genuinely opaque: an outside investor cannot verify the mortality assumptions, and that opacity is a permanent part of the discount.
highlights: EPS +159.6% year over year - driven by investment yield expansion, not premium volume
Revenue +18.5%
Forward P/E of approximately 8.3x - the cheapest name scoring above 93 on the entire scan
Rising Treasury yields are a direct and durable margin tailwind on the float
Global diversification across US, Asian and European mortality books

accomplishments: Delivered EPS growth of 159.6% while trading at a single-digit forward multiple

analyses.name: Howmet Aerospace Inc.
analyses.verdict: Tied for the highest score on the scan and the purest aerospace-cycle asset in the market - a 52-week high with revenue up 24.1% and EPS up 33.0%, though the 45.7x multiple and 0.82x volume are the honest caveats.

financials.period: Last completed fiscal year (FY2025, ended December 2025)
financials.summary: Howmet manufactures engineered fasteners, turbine airfoils and forged aluminium wheels - components that are individually small and collectively impossible to substitute, because they are qualified into specific aircraft and engine programmes over years. That qualification barrier is the entire economic moat, and it is why revenue growth of 24.1% converted to EPS growth of 33.0%: pricing power on qualified content flows almost directly to margin. Demand comes from two distinct sources that rarely weaken simultaneously - commercial aircraft build rates recovering toward pre-disruption levels, and defense programmes whose funding just received a geopolitical reminder. The aftermarket spares business is the highest-margin element and grows with the installed fleet's flying hours rather than with new deliveries, which smooths the cycle considerably. The 45.7x forward multiple is the clear weakness in the case: this is priced as a secular growth company rather than a cyclical supplier.

analyses.name: RTX Corporation
analyses.verdict: The direct defense expression of the Iran headline, and unusually one where the fundamentals were already working before the headline arrived - a 52-week high on above-average volume with revenue up 14.5% and EPS up 28.7%.

financials.period: Last completed fiscal year (FY2025, ended December 2025)
financials.summary: RTX combines three businesses with different economics: Pratt & Whitney engines, Collins Aerospace systems, and Raytheon missiles and defense. That mix is the point - the commercial aerospace side gives it aftermarket revenue tied to flying hours, while the defense side gives it a multi-year funded backlog that is largely insensitive to the economic cycle. Revenue growth of 14.5% converting to EPS growth of 28.7% reflects margin recovery in the engine business after a period of costly powder-metal inspections, plus favourable mix as higher-margin defense and aftermarket revenue grew faster than original equipment. The backlog is the most important disclosure in the business: it converts to revenue over years and gives visibility that almost no momentum name possesses. The 28.7x forward multiple is full for a defense prime historically, and reflects the market pricing in an elevated threat environment.

analyses.name: Dell Technologies Inc.
analyses.verdict: AI infrastructure exposure at 21.2x forward earnings with revenue up 87.5% - and the one place in the AI complex TradingView still rates BUY while it hands SELL ratings to the semiconductors.

financials.period: Last completed fiscal year (FY2026, ended January 2026)
financials.summary: Dell's numbers are extraordinary at the top line and require care underneath it. Revenue growth of 87.5% and EPS growth of 282.5% are driven by AI server demand at a scale that has transformed the company's revenue base within roughly two years. The critical nuance is margin: AI servers carry structurally thinner gross margins than Dell's traditional infrastructure or client businesses, because the value in the box sits largely in the accelerators Dell buys rather than the integration it adds. So revenue growth of 87.5% is not as valuable per dollar as the same growth would be elsewhere, and the EPS growth is flattered by operating leverage on a fixed cost base rather than by margin expansion. What makes the stock work anyway is the 21.2x forward multiple - a fraction of what the market pays for the semiconductor layer of the same trade. Dell is also a genuine dual business: the traditional infrastructure and PC segments provide cash flow independent of the AI cycle.

analyses.name: Science Applications International Corporation
analyses.verdict: The only technology name TradingView rates STRONG BUY - and it earns that by not really being a technology stock at all: government services at 11.4x forward earnings, 0.6% from a 52-week high while the sector is sold.

financials.period: Last completed fiscal year (FY2026, ended January 2026)
financials.summary: SAIC provides technical, engineering and IT services to US federal agencies, principally defense and intelligence customers. The economics are entirely unlike the technology sector it is classified in: revenue arrives through multi-year contracts with a customer that does not reduce spending in a recession, and margins are contractually constrained rather than expandable at will. That explains the number that matters most in this year's results - EPS growth of 83.8% against revenue growth of only 1.5%. The revenue line is essentially flat, so the entire earnings expansion came from margin discipline, portfolio pruning of low-margin contracts, and share count reduction through buybacks. That is a legitimate but finite source of growth: you cannot cut and repurchase your way to compounding indefinitely. The 11.4x forward multiple prices exactly that concern, and it is why SAIC is the cheapest technology name scoring above 90 on the entire scan.

journey_52w.summary: SAIC rose from roughly 92 at the 52-week low to 125.95, and the notable feature is that it did so on a completely different driver from everything around it. The technology sector's year was an AI capex story, and SAIC has no exposure to it whatsoever - its advance came from margin execution and from a defense-services demand environment that firmed as global threats multiplied. That independence is exactly why it is at a 52-week high in a week when Technology converted only 29 of 79 names to a STRONG BUY signal and TradingView issued SELL ratings across the chip complex.

analyses.name: SpaceX
analyses.verdict: NEW LISTING - the quant signals are blank rather than favourable, so this is a business judgment, not a chart judgment: an unmatched launch and satellite-broadband franchise still in active price discovery.

financials.period: No full fiscal year has been reported as a public company
financials.summary: This is the single most important caveat on the whole brief: SpaceX has not yet reported a complete fiscal year under public disclosure rules, so there is no audited full-year income statement to narrate. What can be said about the business model without inventing numbers is this. Revenue comes from two very different engines. The launch business sells rides to orbit to commercial satellite operators, national space agencies and defense customers, and its economics rest on booster reusability - refurbishing and reflying a first stage rather than expending it is what separates its cost per kilogram from every competitor's, and that gap is wide enough that most rivals do not attempt to price against it. The second engine, Starlink, is a consumer and enterprise broadband subscription business, and it is the one that changes the financial character of the company: subscriptions are recurring, they scale with satellites already in orbit, and they convert a lumpy project-revenue business into something closer to a utility. The costs are correspondingly heavy - constellation replenishment is a permanent capital expense, since satellites deorbit and must be replaced continuously. Investors should treat every specific valuation or margin figure circulating about this company with caution until the first full public report; the honest position today is that the model is understood and the numbers are not yet disclosed on a comparable basis.
highlights: NEW LISTING - no full fiscal year reported as a public company; no audited annual figures to cite
Two revenue engines: project-based launch services and recurring Starlink subscriptions
Booster reusability is the structural cost advantage underpinning launch economics
Constellation replenishment is a permanent, recurring capital expense, not a one-time build
The first full quarterly report will be the first genuine disclosure of Starlink unit economics

accomplishments: Achieved and sustained a launch cadence no other Western operator approaches
Established orbital booster reuse as routine rather than experimental, resetting industry cost structures
Built Starlink into a global consumer and enterprise broadband network with a substantial subscriber base
Completed a public listing that made a formerly private asset accessible to public market investors

journey_52w.summary: There is no 52-week journey to narrate - SPCX has only weeks of public trading history, which is precisely why the scan flags it is_new_listing and why its 52-week, VCP and relative-strength signals come back blank. The short history that does exist reads as a textbook IPO arc: an initial enthusiasm phase to a post-listing high near 211, a give-back of roughly 49% to a floor near 108, and a stabilisation to the current 143.34, about 1% above its short-term 50-day. That pattern is normal price discovery for a heavily anticipated listing, not a signal about the business. It also means overhead supply from early buyers sits between here and the high, and lock-up expiries have not yet run their course.

critical.valuation: There is no honest valuation to state. Without a full reported fiscal year there is no earnings base, and there is no public comparable for a company that is simultaneously the dominant launch provider and a global satellite broadband operator. Anyone quoting a precise multiple here is quoting an estimate. The rational position is to treat position size as the risk control rather than the entry price, and to wait for the first full report before treating any valuation figure as real.
